graphEvents.label: Which plain rows miss because a hub defers or routes to a command-less mode
All five delivered plain offers travel through a compiled hub route or the doctor handoff

label: The chat set has 16 plain tune rows; the after arm delivered 5 offers (3 create, 2 doctor helper) and none on 11, while the capture marks 6 offered because it counts top-3 command presence and the renderer prints only the top plus a doctor companion.

Every delivered plain offer travels through a compiled hub route attached to a top skill or through the doctor helper handoff; no delivered offer comes from a command row outranking its owner on a plain prompt.

On 9 create-family chat rows the sk-doc hub routes single to a command mode on 3, clarifies 1, defers 4 and routes 1 to a command-less quality-control mode, so the hub is the bottleneck on 6 of 9 rather than the attach layer.

Hub vocabulary is paraphrase-blind: it matches the corpus phrasing that already passes and misses ordinary rewordings such as agent definition, persona file, document before and after my rewrite, overview page and hub skill, so each miss falls to defer.

The deep family misses twice: the deep hub defers on the research row, the review row's top sk-code route lands on a command-less sk-code-review mode, and the doctor-deep-loop row routes to research but the depth gate suppresses it while no doctor mode exists.

The smallest hub-side rule is paraphrase alias widening plus a defer-time offer restricted to the leading mode's ask or read-only run command, never a start command, with none of the proposed phrases present in the 31 readable none rows.
